facts.statement: Researchers created a new cell model of Krabbe disease by using CRISPR technology to remove the GALC gene in human oligodendrocyte cells.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The modified cells had significantly lower levels of GALC gene transcripts and enzyme activity compared to normal cells.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Cells lacking the GALC enzyme built up high levels of two specific lipids called psychosine and lactosylceramide.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Brain and heart tissue from twitcher mice, a common animal model for this disease, also showed increased levels of lactosylceramide.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The study found that changes in lactosylceramide levels were connected to altered activity in the AKT cellular signaling pathway in both the cells and the mice.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The results suggest that lactosylceramide buildup is a consistent feature of GALC deficiency in both human cell models and animal models.
facts.subject: other
